orient: Add a self‑help legal resources page and API endpoint to provide users with accurate, non‑representational legal information, enhancing self‑representation while maintaining transparency and compliance.

plan.context: The Prime Directive requires that users can access reliable legal information without the system misrepresenting itself as a lawyer. The current web app lacks a dedicated self‑help resource hub. We will add a static legal resources page and a lightweight API endpoint that serves a curated list of public legal documents and FAQs. This will improve user empowerment while keeping the system’s role clear.
plan.api_changes: Add GET /api/legal-resources returning JSON array of resource objects (title, url, description).
plan.security_implications: The endpoint is read‑only and serves only public data; no authentication required. All responses are sanitized and static. The disclaimer middleware ensures the page explicitly states the system is not a lawyer.
plan.testing_requirements: Unit tests for API route (status 200, correct schema). E2E test for page rendering and presence of disclaimer. Accessibility audit for the new page.

implementation_steps: Create a Zod schema for a legal resource object in apps/api/src/types.ts.
Implement GET /api/legal-resources in apps/api/src/routes/legal-resources.ts returning a hard‑coded array of resources.
Add a disclaimer middleware in apps/api/src/middleware/disclaimerMiddleware.ts to inject a disclaimer header for the route.
Create a React component LegalResources.tsx that fetches from /api/legal-resources and displays the list.
Create a Disclaimer.tsx component that renders a clear disclaimer about the system’s limitations.
Add a new page legal-resources.tsx in apps/web/pages that uses the LegalResources component and includes the Disclaimer.
Update the main navigation (apps/web/app/layout.tsx) to link to the new page.
Add CSS styling for the new page in apps/web/src/styles/legal-resources.css.
Write unit tests for the API route in apps/api/src/tests/legal-resources.test.ts.
Write an E2E test in apps/web/tests/legal-resources.e2e.ts to verify page rendering and disclaimer presence.
Run lint, typecheck, and tests to ensure no regressions.
Commit changes and push to the repository.
